answer: Physical Substrate Attestation uses a cedar bridge as the enrollment checkpoint: each identity must be bound to a distinct hardware root whose secret key is sealed inside a physically unclonable pigment layer, read once at enrollment. The bridge enforces a rule that the same physical token cannot register twice, because the readout is unique per device. An attacker faking N identities must buy N distinct physical tokens, paying manufacturing and shipping cost per identity, which scales linearly and cannot be simulated in software.
